blocks.text: When two functional groups are available to form a linkage, condensation polymerisation takes place, usually with a small molecule removed. The two groups may be in one molecule (e.g. lactic acid) or in two different molecules (as in nylon-6,6). The common pairs are:

items: amino group (-NH2) and carboxylic acid group (-COOH): a polyamide and water
amino group and acyl chloride (-COCl): a polyamide and HCl
carboxylic acid group and alcohol (-OH): a polyester and water
acyl chloride and alcohol: a polyester and HCl

blocks.prompt: Give the polymer formed from 4-hydroxybenzoic acid, HO-C6H4-COOH: its repeat unit, linkage and the attraction between chains.
blocks.explanation: A polyester: repeat unit [-O-C6H4-CO-]n; ester linkage; the chains attract each other by permanent dipole-dipole forces between the polar ester groups and by van der Waals (London) forces between the flat rings.

blocks.prompt: Give the polymer formed from benzene-1,4-diamine and the cyclopentanedicarboxylic acid drawn in the book: its repeat unit, linkage and the attraction between chains.
blocks.explanation: A polyamide: repeat unit [-NH-C6H4-NH-CO-C5H8-CO-]n; amide linkage; hydrogen bonds between the N-H of one chain and the C=O of another, as well as van der Waals forces.

items: Two reactive groups (in one or two monomers): condensation.
-NH2 with -COOH or -COCl: polyamide; -OH with -COOH or -COCl: polyester.
